hints.text: The power is not alone yet. Get $2^x$ by itself before thinking about the exponent.
Divide both sides by $3$ to get $2^x = 32$. Then write $32$ as a power of $2$.

explanation: Remove the multiplier before working on the exponent, because the same-base method needs the power alone.
Dividing both sides of the equation by $3$ gives $2^x = 32$.
Since $32 = 2^5$, the exponents match and $x = 5$. Checking the original equation, $3 \times 2^5 = 3 \times 32 = 96$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Take the log of both sides
steps: Take $\log_2$ of both sides — the exponent slides down: $x = \log_2(32)$.
